title: Weekly Markets Monitor - All together now
gist: Gold advanced last week despite Fed and BoJ rate hikes, rising yields and a stronger dollar, with gains concentrated in Asian trading hours and ETF inflows positive across all regions, leading the World Gold Council to endorse the view that gold demand has become broad-based and structural rather than purely rate/dollar-driven.

themes.theme: Gold's Decoupling From Rates and the Dollar

insights.claim: Gold extended its advance last week even though the Fed and BoJ both hiked rates, bond yields rose, and the US dollar strengthened — a combination that has historically pressured gold lower.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Classic macro headwinds for gold (higher rates, stronger dollar) failed to stop the rally, signaling investors should question reliance on rate/dollar correlations to time gold entries and exits.
insights.quote: Two separate central bank hikes, rising yields and a stronger dollar did not dent gold’s advance last week
insights.locator: Two separate central bank hikes, rising yields

insights.claim: World Gold Council's intraday sessions data show gold's price gains last week were concentrated during Asian market trading hours, pointing to Asia-based buying as a key driver of the move.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Investors tracking what is driving gold should watch Asian demand flows rather than assume Western rates-desk trading is dominating price action.
insights.quote: Our sessions data show prices climbed mostly during Asian market hours.
insights.locator: Our sessions data show prices climbed

insights.claim: Gold ETF flows were positive across all regions last week, according to the Council's GRAM weekly attribution data.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Broad-based regional ETF buying rather than a single-region trade corroborates the thesis of widespread, structural gold demand.
insights.quote: Gold ETF flows meanwhile, were positive across regions, evident in GRAM’s weekly attribution.
insights.locator: Gold ETF flows meanwhile, were positive

insights.claim: The World Gold Council endorses an FT Unhedged observation that gold is now being driven by broad-based, structural conviction across every category of market participant, rather than by any single trading cohort.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: If demand truly spans central banks, ETF investors, retail and institutions simultaneously, gold's floor may be sturdier than positioning-based models suggest, favoring a structural rather than tactical allocation stance.
insights.quote: we broadly agree with an observation from FT Unhedged this morning that gold is now driven by “broad-based, structural conviction across every category of market participant”.
insights.locator: we broadly agree with an observation from FT Unhedged

insights.claim: If gold's rally is indeed being driven by structural, broad-based conviction rather than tactical positioning, the metal may at times decouple from its traditional sensitivity to moves in yields and the dollar.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Traders relying on real-yield or dollar-index correlations for gold signals should stress-test those models against periods where gold decouples from them.
insights.quote: If so, gold may at times become less sensitive to the vagaries of yield and dollar moves.
insights.locator: If so, gold may at times

themes.theme: Central Bank Divergence and Inflation Pressure

insights.claim: The Federal Reserve and the Bank of Japan both raised interest rates last week while the Bank of England held, making central bank policy divergence the dominant market theme of the week.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Simultaneous Fed and BoJ hikes alongside a BoE hold mark a notable divergence in G-major policy paths that could drive cross-asset and currency volatility going forward.
insights.quote: Central bank policy was the dominant theme last week, with the Fed and BoJ hiking and the BoE holding.
insights.locator: Central bank policy was the dominant theme

insights.claim: Escalating tensions in the Middle East heightened concerns over oil supply disruptions last week, adding to inflationary pressure at a time when inflation was already firming in the Eurozone, UK, Japan and India.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: A geopolitically-driven oil supply-shock risk stacking on top of already-firming global inflation supports continued demand for inflation hedges like gold.
insights.quote: escalating tensions in the Middle East heightened concerns over oil supply disruptions, adding to inflationary pressures as inflation firmed in the Eurozone, UK, Japan and India.
insights.locator: At the same time, escalating tensions

themes.theme: US Resilience Versus China's Uneven Growth

insights.claim: The US economy showed continued resilience last week on strong retail sales and fewer jobless claims, even as China's data pointed to uneven growth, with export- and technology-led sectors strong but domestic demand weak.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: The US-China growth divergence — a resilient US consumer versus soft Chinese domestic demand — matters for relative-value positioning and for gauging global growth momentum into year-end.
insights.quote: the US economy continued to show resilience, led by strong retail sales and fewer jobless claims, while China's updates pointed to continued uneven growth, with export- and technology-led sectors remaining strong while domestic demand stayed weak.
insights.locator: Meanwhile, the US economy continued to show resilience

insights.claim: Despite the hawkish central bank moves, broader risk markets behaved conventionally last week: major global equity markets ended lower, bond yields edged higher, the dollar strengthened, and oil eased marginally but stayed elevated — a contrast to gold's non-conforming advance.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: That conventional markets moved as textbook macro logic predicted while gold alone broke pattern reinforces the case that gold's move was demand-driven rather than macro-beta driven.
insights.quote: Major global equity markets ended the week lower, bond yields edged higher, the US dollar strengthened and oil prices eased marginally but stayed elevated.
insights.locator: Major global equity markets ended the week lower
